title: Great concept, unreliable sync
body:
The Streaks app offers a fantastic concept for habit tracking, but its execution falls short. Synchronisation between the Apple Watch, iPhone, and Mac is frustratingly unreliable. Tasks completed on the Apple Watch frequently fail to update on other devices, and activity ring progress doesn’t show correctly on the watch. Likewise Mac or iPhone to the watch. 

This is particularly disappointing given that iCloud sync is enabled on all devices, background app refresh is on, and the devices are connected to fast, reliable Wi-Fi. Considering the small amount of data being transferred when a task is completed, the sync issues are difficult to excuse.

Support was unhelpful, even infering they don’t have an Apple Watch for testing. While the idea is solid, the app's poor sync and lack of refinement make it hard to recommend in its current state.

title: Useful For My Needs & Good Price But With Slight Annoyances
body:
Useful app that wasn’t too expensive or had a subscription. I can’t remember things easily so I wanted a way to add reminders to my phone so that they would remind me all day and count different meditations etc using the Dynamic Island and Lock Screen as a permanent reminder.

Unfortunately while this app does seem to use the Dynamic Island it (as far as I can tell) is only if you are currently running a time based Streak that has a timer that has actually been started. You can’t manually choose to keep a reminder or a none time based Streak in the Dynamic Island or in a persistent notification to remind yourself throughout the day.

The lock screen medication countdowns are useful ie so I can see that I have 3 of 4 tablets left today etc but it’s a bit annoying having multiple and not being able to specify which ones I want to see and when.

I found a slight workaround that involves using different pages for different streaks and then hiding the ones that I don’t need to see so that they won’t show on my Lock Screen or in widgets etc, but I think that’s more annoying than just being able to use a menu option to exclude certain Streaks from your screen.

Same goes for manually updating ones with multiple sections throughout the day like if I forgot to log 3 tablets then why I can’t just manually set the amount instead of having to manually press it for each missed time, which is even more annoying when you make a mistake and have to go through even more unnecessary steps to undo and then redo it all again…

I really hope this is possible in a future update because it seems easy enough to do considering the current settings allow for certain Streaks that persist on your screen, widgets, notifications and in the Dynamic Island but you get little control over how and when and which are shown without hiding them completely.

Despite this I still found the widgets useful and visual enough that they work as great reminders throughout the day and useful logs over time and I can quickly visualise how many tablets I have taken / are remaining and see it on my Apple Watch.

I love the Shortcuts integration too which fit right into an existing Shortcut I had made to log medication. Before I had struggled to find a way to log my total daily dose and then to count down every time I logged a tablet and some days I take more which other apps couldn’t handle without ruining the daily amount but Streaks can.

Please expand on this customisation and make it so you can select which streaks to use in the shortcut even if they are completed that day and allow us to manually choose which Streaks appear especially in the Dynamic Island and for how long they persist. If I could do that then this would the perfect app and hopefully with future updates it will be.

title: Much more than a simple task-tracking tool
body:

That’s an achievement by itself, but what really blew me away was how deeply customisable, flexible, and powerful the app is if you take a bit of time to dive into the menus and explore what it’s really capable of: custom task scheduling, automatic reminders, finding trends in completion data, the list of features goes on and on.

One of the very few apps I use every day, and I’ve come to rely on Streaks to manage much of my day-to-day work both personally and professionally. 

Absolute gem of an app.

body: As someone who has dedicated much of my personal, academic & professional life researching into the flow state, I can unquestionably say this is my favourite app… ever! Every day I wake up to the same blank slate, then tick off my vitamins and supplements, it automatically registers when I’ve used my Bluetooth scales, and then it’s workout time, I burn 700 calories before I sit at my computer ( which is ok when I’m nearly touching 70 in a couple of weeks) then I tick off ‘homework’, two sets of three pomodoro sessions, three sets of twenty minutes of reading/studying… oh and I take at least one photo before I go home, where I check off some house cleaning and two sessions of playing a musical instrument… oh and it also tracks when I wash my hands, so I set a minimum of seven times a day. I only just discovered that it also has some fantastic watch faces which I have just installed. These are just my preferences but there are loads to choose from, many of them no brainers and all of them allowing you to set an easily achievable threshold and see it slowly increase automatically over the forthcoming weeks and months. Guys, if you wanna beta tester, I’m well up for it, you may even convince me to save up for one of these new VR headsets… I can’t imagine how good this app will be when you’re wearing one of those!

title: More screens is a must for some users
body:
I appreciate the ideal of focusing on only 12 habits and can see that some UI currently hinges on the two screens. But it feels arbitrary to not have the option to add additional screens if I need them, and the option would do no harm to anyone that can manage with the default two screens.

Alongside other habits, I wanted to track weekly streaks for running, cycling and swimming targets, but tracking their streaks individually uses up a quarter of all my slots. Why should someone that runs three days a week have more other habit slots to track with than someone that does three different exercises per week? I also wanted to track sleep as when I go to bed and when I wake up, rather than just overall time so I can see where I’m missing my targets. I find that habits work for me when I can focus on specific details, but I’m having to generalise or cut other things out to make space.

I really like the way the app works in general, and to be honest I’d pay for additional screens or a second instance of the same app just to track what I want. Compromising on what details I can track is a real frustration though, and I do regret paying for it at the moment rather than finding an app with no limits. I’ve already spent time setting up shortcuts and some habits so I’ll cross my fingers for an improvement while I test out other apps for a secondary/replacement tracker.

- 
Review besides the bug below:

The concept of streaks is really solid to form habits. It’s a psychological hack, yes, but something that works for me. Mind you an app is not as powerful as a poster in a room, but its the next best thing.

I have had a few apps which track streaks, and this app, Streaks, definitely has the best design that actually is close to checking out things on a poster. And UI really is important to promote usage and habit building.

The cool things which this app does differently which stood out for me:
1: you can set timers for timed activities like 1 hour study or 15 min meditation.
2. Multiple tasks which form an activity can be broken down. For e.g, drinking 10 glasses of water can be checked off one glass at a time.
3. There’s a tie in to health app so you don’t need to check off workouts and other health things.

Overall happy with this app and see myself using it. I have had a few streaks going the last couple of months, but have not been consistent enough. Hope that will change in the coming months.

body: I found this at just the right time. I tried it a while ago but didn’t really get into it. Now, combined with a genuine desire to create better habits, this app is really coming into its own. This may be controversial, and I can see the reasons behind having only 12. So, perhaps a compromise add functionality without tempting the user to create too many habits at once could be the ability to group clusters of related habits together. For example, I am trying to develop a reading habit for both fiction and non-fiction and so I have both of these as habits to track. If I could, for example, click on “reading“ and have two connected habits open up as options, that would be really cool. At the moment, one can create clusters of habits by, for example, calling the habit “read fiction, read non-fiction“ and just putting the habit as two sessions per day, but that is crude and unwieldy and doesn’t show if you missed one and not the other. Habit clusters would be awesome. Anyway, that would be the improvement I would really like to see, and that would make the tracker even more useful than it already is.

I’ve found that most others you have to set a time to be notified, and I’ve never found that helpful as I start to expect it so get into the habit of ignoring it, whereas because this app decides when to notify me it feels like a genuine reminder.  Such a simple thing, yet so important. I like how customisable it is too, with all of the different icons, and how it integrates with my Apple Watch. I also appreciate that it’s a one time payment only, as I refuse to purchase subscriptions as it’s a rip off. 

The only downside to the app for me is that I expected it to be a little more goals oriented, which is probably just my misunderstanding but it is a small disappointment. I thought I’d be able to use it to plan out and track my progress towards large goals, but it’s basically a habit tracker.

In my opinion, adding 6 streaks straight off the bat is a bad idea. It will be almost impossible, as i figured out myself, to start 6 streaks in one go. It is far better to start one or two streaks and add more as the initial streaks become engrained into your day to day life.

title: Good app
body:

Pros:
• iCloud sync.
• Broad Health support for automatic completion of tasks.
• Extensive (notification & theme) customisation.
• Universal app support (iPad, iPhone, Watch).

Technical limitation?:
• Health data retrieval (& sync) requires specifically launching the iPhone version of the app, not iPad or Watch.

Cons:
• The interface can be quite opaque, with ‘…’ buttons everywhere.
• No iCloud sync for per-task notification settings.
• Some bugs. (With Health sleep data permission granted - adding a sleep duration task works fine, but the wake & sleep task says no data is available and doesn't update from Health)

title: Good, but could be better
body:
Don't get me wrong, this is a good app for making good habits. It makes it easy to mark a habit as complete so that it isn't a chore to keep track of.

It isn't very good at tracking bad habits though. I would expect a better way of tracking when you have not done something, as if you were trying to break a bad habit. All you would need to do is reverse the colours for bad habits, so you mark off when you have done something you shouldn't have, by the end of the week you will be able to see how often you did the bad habit, and will be able to see how you progress over time. 

It also doesn't make much sense to limit the number of tasks to 6. I know many people won't need to track more than that but what if they do? It seems kinda arbitrary to have a limit like this. I assume it is something to do with fitting all of the buttons in the today widget, but surely you could add as many as you like in the app and just mark up to 6 to be shown in the today widget?

Anyway, those are my suggestions. It's a good app, but I can see where it could be improved.

title: Motivates and regulates
body:

The idea is that you can set targets to achieve (mine are all daily) and you can work towards them during the day however you please. Then every time you manage to achieve the target by the time you set, you build up your streak. The best thing, for me, is the flexibility compared to usual timetable type apps! 

Because you're doing things daily, it also regulates your daily activities, which is a helpful bonus. 

I should mention though that I got this app free from a Starbucks card, so with that in consideration, I have no complaints!

title: Backtrack?
body:
It's an awesome app. Really simple and easy to use.
You can use it to aim for daily tasks or set it for only certain days or number of days per week. An improvement would be the option of aiming for twice a day.
It would also be good if you could pull up a calendar and record for previous days so that if you've forgotten to log it but have done the task, then you don't lose your streak. Or be able to say 'my current streak is two days' when you create a new task. I understand that 6 is a good amount of habits for most people, and the option for too many would be overwhelming but I use it to track the most basic things (shower, clean teeth, etc) so having a few more would be good. Maybe 8 (4 rows of 2) or 9 (3 rows of 3) so that they still all fit on the same page.

title: Simple and very effective
body:
This is a brilliant app, especially when used with the Apple Watch complication. It's a very simple and effective way of monitoring your daily habits and ensuring you get them done. Basically this app will improve your life. Not bad for a couple of quid! 

The health kit integration works well, although I would like a bit more granularity in the goals you can set- eg being able to choose a target of 4500 steps rather than just 4000 or 5000. Also, the only frustration I have with the Apple Watch compilation is that it doesn't seem to auto update health data connected habits unless you open the iPhone app first. 

As someone who likes to tinker, I'd like to be able to try out other habits to track without having to delete one of my six current habits (and all their historical data) first. 

And possibly I'd also like the ability to put habits on hold for a holiday. Maybe make it so that the minimum hold length is 5 days. I'm not expecting to go to bed on time, read every day, run every day, on my holiday, so I don't really want to feel bad about not completing them... But maybe this suggested hold period be too tempting for some people. 

Long story short it's excellent, and only a few minor minor things above would make it perfect.
